# Introduction

This chapter covers fractional factorial designs, Bayesian-inspired designs, and mixture designs.

**Citation**: V. R. Joseph (2026). *Experimental Design for Data Science and Engineering*. CRC Press.

```{r libraries, message=FALSE}
library(rkriging)
library(HiGarrote)
```

# Section 8.1: Two-level Designs

## Half-normal Plot

```{r halfnormal, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
A <- rep(c(-1, 1), c(4, 4))
B <- rep(rep(c(-1, 1), c(2, 2)), 2)
C <- rep(c(-1, 1), 4)
D <- A * B * C

y <- c(504, 984, 928, 808, 992, 784, 464, 976)
a <- lm(y ~ (A + B + C)^3)

eff <- a$coef[-1]
names(eff) <- c("1", "2", "3", "12", "13", "23", "123")
I <- length(eff)
u <- qnorm(0.5 + 0.5 * (1:I - 0.5) / I)
saeff <- sort(abs(eff))

par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
plot(u, saeff, type = "n", xlab = "Half-normal Quantiles",
     ylab = "Absolute Coefficients", main = "Half-normal Plot",
     cex.main = 2.5, cex.axis = 1.5, cex.lab = 1.5, xlim = c(0, max(u) + 0.1))
text(u, saeff, names(saeff), cex = 1.5, col = c(rep(4, 4), rep(2, 3)))
```

# Section 8.2: Bayesian-inspired Designs

## Bayesian Half-normal Plot with HiGarrote

```{r bayesian_halfnormal, fig.width=8, fig.height=7}
d <- cbind(A, B, C, D)
a <- Fit.Kriging(d, y, kernel.parameters = list(type = "Gaussian"))
theta <- Get.Kriging.Parameters(a)$lengthscale
mu <- Get.Kriging.Parameters(a)$mu
gam <- (1 - exp(-2^2 / (2 * theta))) / (1 + exp(-2^2 / (2 * theta)))

X <- model.matrix(lm(y ~ (A + B + C + D)^4), data = data.frame(A, B, C, D))
G <- diag(c(model.matrix(lm(1 ~ (gam[1] + gam[2] + gam[3] + gam[4])^4))))
alpha <- G %*% t(X) %*% solve(X %*% G %*% t(X)) %*% (y - mu)
eff <- alpha[-1]
names(eff) <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "12", "13", "14", "23", "24", "34",
                "123", "124", "134", "234", "1234")
I <- length(eff)
u <- qnorm(0.5 + 0.5 * (1:I - 0.5) / I)
saeff <- sort(abs(eff))

par(mar = c(5, 5, 4, 2))
plot(u, saeff, type = "n", xlab = "Half-normal Quantiles",
     ylab = "Absolute Coefficients", main = "Bayesian Half-normal Plot",
     cex.main = 2.5, cex.axis = 1.5, cex.lab = 1.5, xlim = c(0, max(u) + 0.1))
size <- c(rep(1.2, 12), rep(1.5, 3))
text(u, saeff, names(saeff), cex = size, col = c(rep(4, 12), rep(2, 3)))
```

## HiGarrote Variable Selection

```{r higarrote}
cat("HiGarrote Results:\n")
print(HiGarrote(d, y))
```

# Section 8.3: Designs with More than Two Levels

## Orthogonal Arrays (L9, L18)

```{r orthogonal_array}
library(DoE.base)
library(SFDesign)
library(twinning)

full <- full.factorial(4, 3)

# L9 with two replicates
D <- undesign(oa.design(nfactors = 4, nlevels = 3, randomize = FALSE))
D <- data.matrix(D)
D1 <- rbind(D, D)
D1 <- (D1 - 1) / 2
mp1 <- maxpro.crit(D1, delta = 1/3^2) / 3^2
en1 <- energy(full, D1)

# L18
D <- undesign(oa.design(ID = L18, randomize = FALSE))
D <- data.matrix(D)
D2 <- D[, 2:5]
D2 <- (D2 - 1) / 2
mp2 <- maxpro.crit(D2, delta = 1/3^2) / 3^2
en2 <- energy(full, D2)

cat("L9 (2 reps): MaxPro =", round(mp1, 4), ", Energy =", round(en1, 4), "\n")
cat("L18: MaxPro =", round(mp2, 4), ", Energy =", round(en2, 4), "\n")
```

# Section 8.4: Mixture Designs

## Simplex-Lattice and Simplex-Centroid Designs

```{r mixture_designs, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
library(mixexp)
library(Ternary)

D1 <- SLD(3, 2)
D2 <- SCD(3)

par(mar = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

TernaryPlot(axis.labels = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
            atip = expression(x[1]), btip = expression(x[3]), ctip = expression(x[2]),
            alab = "Fraction x1", blab = "Fraction x3", clab = "Fraction x2",
            lab.cex = 1, tip.cex = 2)
TernaryPoints(D1, cex = 3, col = 4, pch = 16)

TernaryPlot(axis.labels = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
            atip = expression(x[1]), btip = expression(x[3]), ctip = expression(x[2]),
            alab = "Fraction x1", blab = "Fraction x3", clab = "Fraction x2",
            lab.cex = 1, tip.cex = 2)
TernaryPoints(D2, cex = 3, col = 4, pch = 16)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## Support Points on Simplex

```{r support_simplex, fig.width=12, fig.height=6}
library(spacefillr)
library(support)

p <- 3
N <- 10000
u <- generate_sobol_set(N, p - 1)
x <- matrix(0, nrow = N, ncol = p)
x[, 1] <- (1 - u[, 1]^(1/2))
x[, 2] <- u[, 1]^(1/2) * (1 - u[, 2])
x[, 3] <- u[, 1]^(1/2) * u[, 2]

set.seed(1)
n <- 11
D1 <- sp(n, p, dist.samp = x)$sp

par(mar = c(0.1, 0.1, 0.1, 0.1))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# Full simplex
TernaryPlot(axis.labels = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
            atip = expression(x[1]), btip = expression(x[3]), ctip = expression(x[2]),
            alab = "Fraction x1", blab = "Fraction x3", clab = "Fraction x2",
            lab.cex = 1, tip.cex = 2)
TernaryPoints(D1, cex = 3, col = 4, pch = 16)

# Constrained region
CAND <- x
C1 <- (x[, 1] + x[, 2] < 0.7)
C2 <- (x[, 1] + x[, 2] > 0.3)
CAND <- CAND[C1 & C2, ]
D2 <- sp(n, p, dist.samp = CAND)$sp

TernaryPlot(axis.labels = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1),
            atip = expression(x[1]), btip = expression(x[3]), ctip = expression(x[2]),
            alab = "Fraction x1", blab = "Fraction x3", clab = "Fraction x2",
            lab.cex = 1, tip.cex = 2)
TernaryPoints(D2, cex = 3, col = 4, pch = 16)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

# Summary

This chapter covered:

1. **Two-level fractional factorial designs** with half-normal plots
2. **Bayesian-inspired designs** using Kriging priors and HiGarrote
3. **Orthogonal arrays** (L9, L18) for multi-level factors
4. **Mixture designs** including SLD, SCD, and support points on simplex
